answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network surveying juniper biomes or tracking sable wildlife can anchor identity generation to cryptographic proof-of-burn. To register a node, an agent must permanently destroy a verifiable quantity of native tokens on-chain. An attacker incurs the scarce, unrecoverable capital cost of incinerating real funds per identity. However, this mechanism imposes systemic deadweight loss and penalizes low-margin, capital-light micro-agents.
